gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Epoch's "11-year" warranty gives free replacement only in years 1–3 and 40% off MSRP in years 4–11, or that LiTime's "5-year" warranty covers the cells only if the battery is fully charged within 7 days of purchase and at least once every 3 months. So the warranty years that brands headline, and that rivals list next to each other, do not mean the same thing.
standout_why: I checked three cited pages. batterytrail.com/posts/lifepo4-rv-battery-spec-database lists warranty years flat (Battle Born 10-year limited, SOK 7-year, LiTime 5 years) and has no Epoch row. boondockmaps.com/rv-power/best-lithium-batteries and vanpowercalc.com both list Epoch as "11 years" with no schedule. None of the three gives the replacement-vs-discount split or LiTime's charging condition. None of them sets out the end-of-life point either: Epoch rates cycles to 80% capacity remaining, while LiTime gives cycles only by depth of discharge (100/80/60%) with no end-of-life point. Batterytrail says makers 'usually' rate to 80%, and vanpowercalc puts LiTime at 80% DoD in its table but 100% DoD in its text. Boondockmaps lists surge figures (200A 30s, 300A 5s, 170A) without saying the time windows make them non-comparable, and batterytrail lists them with no footnote. Vanpowercalc does warn that surge ratings hold only 3–30 s, so that point is only partly new.
decides: This weakens 'long warranty = premium support' as a reason to pay more. Epoch's 11 years is a 3-year replacement warranty followed by a discount coupon. LiTime's 5-year repair-or-replace covers about as many years of free replacement as Epoch's (5 vs 3), on the 230Ah Bluetooth at $530.99 today. That supports ChatGPT's value pick. The catch is that RV owners who store the rig must charge it every 3 months to keep LiTime's cell coverage. I could not open Battle Born's warranty terms, so its 10-year pick can't be confirmed or knocked down on this point.

findings.label: Warranty structure
findings.value: 11-year limited: free replacement in years 1–3, 40% off MSRP on a replacement in years 4–11
findings.note: Register within 90 days or keep proof of purchase. The page states no capacity threshold for a claim. Over the 11-year term, 3 years are full replacement and 8 are a discount.

findings.value: 105 A max continuous (52.5 A / 0.5C recommended sustained); 200 A for up to 10 s
findings.note: Surge window is 10 s, versus LiTime's 1 s rating.

findings.label: Cold charging behaviour
findings.value: Charging disabled at 0 °C / 32 °F, resumes at 5 °C / 41 °F; heater powered by incoming charge current, needs a charger supplying ≥0.5 A; charge range with heating −20 °C to 55 °C (−4 °F to 131 °F)
findings.note: The heater runs only while a charger is connected. It does not draw on stored energy.
